newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- Chartists eye upside for cruising dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Chartists eye upside for cruising dlr/yen.

text.p: A significant rise in dollar/yen on Thursday left the rate poised for additional gains with 118.60/80 and 119.55/60 its initial upside targets, chartists said.

The rate's ability to hold above the 114 level on Friday -- a 61.8 percent fibonnaci retracement of its move from cycle lows of 110.62 to a recent corrective peak of 119.58 -- was an encouraging signal.
But Thursday's move through a key hurdle at 117 yen convinced many that the rate could be headed back above the 120 threshold soon.

"We're bullish ... and today's acceleration really helps our case out," said Drew Baptiste, vice president and technical analyst at J.P. Morgan. "We're constructive looking for it to trade back above 119.55 to 121."

He said the 121 level -- a 61.8 percent retracement of dollar/yen's move down from cycle highs of 127.47 to 110.62 -- would be key and predicted that sustained price action above there would signal a move to fresh multi-year peaks.
Greg Troccoli, director of technical trading strategy at Prudential Securities, said that 118.70 -- a level right between the highs of July 7 and 8 -- would provide initial resistance.

"It's important now for the market to close back above 118.70 for it to break through 120," he said. "If the market can get a close above 118.70 then we could get a move back toward 123.50-125 region."
Troccoli, who called the sharp slide on Friday, August 8 overdone, pegged key support at 114.60 -- a rising trendline originating with the June 11 low of 110.62.
